 Tim Bradley Warns Usyk Against Benavidez Weight Cut
 Larry Jordan - 11/10/2026 - Comments 
 Google News Preferred Source 
 Tim Bradley wants Oleksandr Usyk to force David Benavidez up to heavyweight, warning that dropping back to 200 pounds could backfire down the stretch. While Bradley expects Usyk to control the opening rounds with his southpaw straight left, his concern centers on what occurs once Benavidez absorbs that shot, crashes the pocket, and pins a 39-year-old champion along the cables.
 “You can jab the hell out of him upstairs and downstairs. Yep. Straight left hand down the middle,” Bradley said on his channel. “But if you ain’t got no strength to keep him up off of you, because that’s the thing.”
 Pay attention to Usyk’s foot positioning the instant that straight left connects. In mid-ring, Usyk uses a lead-foot pivot to change the angle before a return volley arrives. Along the perimeter, Benavidez adjusts his base to smother that exit, drives a chopping right into the glove, and whips a left shovel hook underneath the elbow. The moment Usyk plants both heels to shield his ribs, Benavidez uncorks sustained salvos while Usyk hunts for space to reset.
 Bradley highlighted the 233 pounds Usyk scaled against Rico Verhoeven, which sits 33 pounds above the cruiserweight ceiling. Stripping that bulk late in a career exacts a severe metabolic price. Usyk already exhibited heavier feet against Verhoeven. When he halted Tony Bellew in round eight back in 2018, Usyk was 31, naturally acclimated to the division, and possessed the spring to shift gears late. Benavidez presents a much harsher test of whether those 39-year-old legs can execute quick lateral turns after seven rounds of relentless pressure.
 At heavyweight, Usyk preserves the muscle mass he has spent years building. That functional weight allows him to lean on Benavidez, tie up inside exchanges, and sap the challenger’s legs in the clinch. Rather than draining himself on the scale, Usyk holds the championship leverage to force Benavidez to carry unfamiliar bulk over 12 rounds.
